meta.purpose: Ground truth for the apple-ui-craft regression corpus. Each fixture lists the findings a by-the-book review SHOULD produce, in the canonical finding shape from references/review/01-finding-format.md, plus a ruleRef naming the reference section the finding maps to. The scorer (tests/harness/score-review.mjs) matches emitted findings to these labels by ruleRef first, then by the label's owner section cited within eight lines of the labelled line, then by (fixture, dimension) with fuzzy title overlap.
meta.findingShape: id, dimension (a verbatim entry from the dimension registry in references/review/01-finding-format.md), severity (CRITICAL|HIGH|MEDIUM|LOW|NIT), confidence (Hard defect|Quality defect|Pattern smell|Taste note), file, line, title, ruleRef, evidence.
meta.ruleRefConvention: <area>/<defect-slug>, where area is one of meta.ruleRefAreas. Each ruleRef's definition, threshold and severity live in the reference named in that label's `owner` field. Adding a ruleRef here without adding it there is a corpus that tests nothing.
meta.cleanControlRule: A clean control has expected == [] and maxIncidentalFindings == 1: the review may surface at most one incidental note before the control is treated as failed.
meta.severityIsInformational: severity on a label records the reference's by-the-book class; the scorer matches on ruleRef/title, not severity, so a reviewer calling a defect one class higher or lower still counts as a hit.
meta.dimensionCoverage: Labels cover task flow, information architecture, error recovery and state integrity, adaptive layout and Dynamic Type, density and economy, and the platform-conformance checks inside Navigation patterns, Micro-interactions, Layout and spacing, Color system and SF Symbols. Liquid Glass, Typography hierarchy, App icon, Animation, Haptics, VoiceOver and the other accessibility dimensions, performance and platform integration have no labels. Read any pooled recall number as recall over the labelled dimensions, never as coverage of the registry.
meta.swiftFixturesAreReadNotCompiled: Fixtures are read by a reviewing agent, never built. There is no Xcode target, so an editor resolving them against the host macOS SDK will flag iOS-only API (navigationBarTitleDisplayMode, topBarLeading, keyboardType, ContentUnavailableView.search). Those diagnostics are an artifact of having no iOS target and are NOT defects to fix -- several of them ARE the planted defect, and 'fixing' them destroys the fixture.
meta.cleanControlContract: adaptive-clean-control.swift is the guard against the failure mode where a reviewer flags constructs rather than defects -- the mirror image of every other fixture. It uses what the references prescribe: AnyLayout reflow at accessibility sizes, @ScaledMetric on an icon beside text, a reading measure on the detail column, NavigationSplitView at regular width, safeAreaInset for a custom bar, a Codable route, a draft owned above its presentation, interactiveDismissDisabled paired with a real Cancel, a confirmed destructive action, a double-submit guard, a keyboard toolbar, and all five reachable states each with a recovery. A run that flags any of those has learned the wrong lesson and fails the gate here. conformance-clean-control.swift guards the conformance checks the same way: a Toggle restyled through ToggleStyle, a custom dial bridged with accessibilityRepresentation, ignoresSafeArea on the camera preview alone, a required consent step that locks dismissal and says why, a sidebar-adaptable TabView, a drag held in @GestureState, and a custom SF symbol beside system ones.
meta.authored: No fixture is copied from another corpus.

fixtures.note: CLEAN CONTROL. Must produce zero findings. Every construct here is one the references prescribe; flagging any of them means the reviewer is matching constructs rather than defects.

CLEAN CONTROL. A correct review files nothing here; the scorer tolerates one incidental note (maxIncidentalFindings). It holds the prescribed counterpart of every conformance plant, plus the required-step dismiss lock, a restyled Toggle, a Menu whose label is a row's text block restyled plain beside a toolbar Menu that keeps the system chrome on its short Label, a custom dial with accessibilityRepresentation and a custom SF symbol.
